coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: 40 minutes easy, Z2 only—no tempo, no intervals. You're 10 days out and your last three runs all landed at 128–129 bpm average; that's solid maintenance but you don't need sharpness now, you need freshness. Your resting HR dropped to 60 (vs. your 30-day avg of 65.4), which is a clean sign of adaptation, but short sleep (6.55h vs. your 7.63h average) means your nervous system is still catching up. Keep the vert under 400 ft and dial it back to a conversational pace—your body knows the work is done. Save the intensity for race day.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're tapering but not starving. Maintain your daily carb baseline (aim for 5–6 g/kg bodyweight if you're ~80 kg), because glycogen stores matter in a 50K with 2,500 m of vert and sparse aid. Post-run today, prioritize a 3:1 or 4:1 carb-to-protein ratio within 30 minutes—aim for 40–50g carbs and 10–15g protein. Don't drop total calories; drop volume and intensity, not fuel. You'll be carrying your own nutrition in Slovenia, so this week is also your dress rehearsal for race fueling—test your exact aid-station plan (gels, salts, real food if you're using it) on your easy runs.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your limiting factor right now—6.55 hours is 90 minutes short of your average, and at 77% efficiency you're losing quality time. Tonight: no screens after 9 PM, aim for 8.5 hours, and consider a magnesium glycinate 60 minutes before bed if you use it (you likely know your protocol). Your recovery score of 71 is solid, but it could spike to 85+ with two solid nights of 7.5+ hours. Taper weeks are when sleep compounds into race-day readiness; prioritize this over any other recovery modality.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Ten days is the hard part—you're fit, you've done the work, and now your brain wants to doubt the taper. Resist it. Your recent volume (20.6 miles this week vs. 35.6 last week) is exactly where it should be. Spend these ten days visualizing your race strategy: the aid-station locations, your pacing plan for each major climb, and your contingency if conditions go south. Mentally rehearse the descent into Kranjska Gora—that's where most runners blow up. Your fitness is locked in. Taper is about showing up sharp, rested, and confident.
